answer: Trust here flows only along paid work edges. A new seat gains weight when established peers commission real jobs from it; each timber, a signed job receipt worth 1 trust unit, needs a peer-verified result. Weight grows in a spiral: a seat may pass on timbers only up to the units it has earned, so a ring of fakes cannot mint trust from nothing. Admission needs 40 timbers from 10 distinct peers, and each peer's plume, an outgoing budget of 4 timbers per epoch, caps what one patron can lift. 500 fakes need 20,000 real jobs, paid even if never caught.
